description: Model Huffman decoding as a finite-state machine where the state is the current bit-offset within the stream. Rather than enumerating all possible starting states individually, group states into convergence sets - sets of states that will all reach the same state after processing enough input symbols. This reduces redundant computation in parallel FSM execution.
mathematical_formalization: FSM with state space S = {bit_offsets mod block_size}. Transition function delta(s, input_chunk) -> s'. Convergence set CS_i = {s in S : delta^k(s, input[j..j+k]) = delta^k(s', input[j..j+k]) for all s,s' in CS_i after k steps}. CSE computes set->set mappings instead of state->state, achieving 2-8.6x speedup over lookback enumeration.
analogical_connections: Basin of attraction in dynamical systems: different initial conditions converge to same attractor
Consensus protocols in distributed systems: nodes with different initial values converge
implementation_hypothesis: For each DEFLATE block, precompute convergence sets using profiled transition probabilities. During parallel decode, assign segments to threads. Each thread starts with a convergence set rather than a single state. If the set converges to a single state within the segment, no re-execution needed. Otherwise, re-execute with the correct state from the previous segment.
experiment_seed: Implement CSE for DEFLATE Huffman tables. Measure convergence probability vs segment length for typical DEFLATE blocks. Compare parallelization efficiency against naive enumeration (all 15 starting states). Target: >90% convergence within 64 symbols.
